content: Impetigo is a bacterial skin infection that requires targeted treatment based on the extent of the infection, the causative organism, and the patient's age. Below are detailed treatment recommendations for both adults and pediatric patients: Impetigo in Adults 1. Empiric Antimicrobial Therapy: For cases with a limited number of lesions, the preferred treatment is either mupirocin applied topically twice daily for 5 days or retapamulin applied topically twice daily for 5 days. For cases with numerous lesions or outbreaks associated with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, systemic therapy is recommended. The preferred regimens include: Dicloxacillin 250 mg orally four times daily for 7 days. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg orally twice daily for 7 days. Cephalexin 250 mg orally four times daily for 7 days. For patients allergic to penicillin, alternative regimens include: Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 7 days. Clindamycin 300–400 mg orally four times daily for 7 days. Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 1–2 double-strength tablets orally twice daily for 7 days. 2. Culture-Directed Antimicrobial Therapy: If the infection is caused by Streptococcus alone, the preferred treatment is penicillin V 250–500 mg orally four times daily for 7 days. For penicillin-allergic patients, alternatives include: Erythromycin 250 mg orally four times daily for 7 days. Clindamycin 300–400 mg orally four times daily for 7 days. If the infection is caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), the preferred regimens include: Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 7 days. Clindamycin 300–450 mg orally four times daily for 7 days. Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 1–2 double-strength tablets orally twice daily for 7 days. Impetigo in Pediatric Patients 1. Empiric Antimicrobial Therapy: For cases with a limited number of lesions, the preferred treatment is either mupirocin applied topically twice daily for 5 days or retapamulin applied topically twice daily for 5 days. For cases with numerous lesions or outbreaks associated with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, systemic therapy is recommended. The preferred regimens include: Amoxicillin-clavulanate at a dose of 25 mg/kg/day (based on the amoxicillin component) orally twice daily for 7 days. Cephalexin at a dose of 25–50 mg/kg/day orally divided into three to four doses daily for 7 days. For penicillin-allergic patients, alternative regimens include: Clindamycin at a dose of 25–30 mg/kg/day orally divided into three doses daily for 7 days. Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim at a dose of 8–12 mg/kg/day orally divided into two doses daily for 7 days. 2. Culture-Directed Antimicrobial Therapy: If the infection is caused by Streptococcus alone, the preferred treatment is penicillin V at a dose of 60,000–100,000 units/kg orally four times daily for 7 days. For penicillin-allergic patients, alternatives include: Erythromycin at a dose of 40 mg/kg/day orally divided into three to four doses daily for 7 days. Clindamycin at a dose of 20 mg/kg/day orally divided into three doses daily for 7 days. If the infection is caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), the preferred regimens include: Clindamycin at a dose of 25–30 mg/kg/day orally divided into three doses daily for 7 days. Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim at a dose of 8–12 mg/kg/day orally divided into two doses daily for 7 days.
